subtitle: Out Cebu · Philippine Airlines
overview: A one-way journey across central Japan, flying Philippine Airlines into Tokyo and home from Osaka. See Tokyo, take a Lake Ashi cruise in Hakone, visit Lake Kawaguchi and the Kubota Itchiku Art Museum, Matsumoto Castle, Takayama Old Town, Shirakawa-go village, Kyoto’s Arashiyama and Golden Pavilion, Nara Deer Park and Osaka Castle. Seven nights in 3-star hotels with an English-speaking guide.
travelDatesNote: Departures from Cebu, Nov 26–Dec 3 2026 to Nov 26–Dec 3 2026. The rate changes by date: an amount on a date is added to the base rate per pax. Seats are limited and confirmed at booking.

placeDesc.Shibuya Crossing: The famous busy pedestrian scramble crossing in front of Shibuya Station.
placeDesc.Hachiko Statue: A bronze statue of the loyal dog Hachiko outside Shibuya Station, a popular meeting spot.
placeDesc.Asakusa Temple: Sensoji, Tokyo's oldest temple, reached through the Kaminarimon gate and Nakamise shopping street.
placeDesc.Tokyo Skytree: Tokyo's tall broadcasting tower near Asakusa, seen here on a photo stop.
placeDesc.Odaiba Rainbow Bridge: A suspension bridge over Tokyo Bay, with views of the Odaiba waterfront.
placeDesc.Lake Ashi: A scenic crater lake in Hakone with views of Mt. Fuji on clear days, crossed on a cruise.
placeDesc.Lake Kawaguchi: One of the Fuji Five Lakes, famed for reflections and views of Mt. Fuji.
placeDesc.Kubota Itchiku Art Museum: A museum by Lake Kawaguchi showing the kimono art of Itchiku Kubota, in a garden setting.
placeDesc.Matsumoto Castle: One of Japan's best-preserved original castles, known as the Crow Castle for its black walls.
placeDesc.Takayama Old Town: A well-preserved old merchant district of Takayama with wooden houses, sake breweries and shops.
placeDesc.Hida Folk Village: An open-air museum near Takayama of old thatched-roof farmhouses moved from the Hida region.
placeDesc.Shirakawa-go: A UNESCO World Heritage village of steep-roofed gassho-zukuri farmhouses in the mountains.
placeDesc.Arashiyama Bamboo Grove: A path through tall bamboo in Kyoto's Arashiyama district, one of the city's most photographed spots.
placeDesc.Golden Pavilion: Kinkaku-ji, Kyoto's Zen temple covered in gold leaf and reflected in its pond.
placeDesc.Gion District: Kyoto's historic geisha district of wooden teahouses and lantern-lit lanes.
placeDesc.Nara Deer Park: A park in Nara where friendly free-roaming deer live near Todai-ji and other temples.
placeDesc.Osaka Castle: A landmark castle in Osaka with a white tower and stone-walled moats, seen on a photo stop.
placeDesc.Shinsaibashi: Osaka's long covered shopping arcade with department stores, boutiques and shops.
placeDesc.Dotonbori: Osaka's neon-lit canal-side entertainment and food street, famous for street food.
